newsitem.title: GERMANY: Koebnick - Buba statement to be brief, worth reading.
newsitem.headline: Koebnick - Buba statement to be brief, worth reading.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick said on Wednesday that the Bundesbank's statement commenting on the German government's plans to revalue the central bank's reserves would be "worth reading and brief".
Koebnick told reporters at a reception the statement, due to be released at 1700 GMT, would contain no surprises, "although some may be surprised at it," he added.
The Bundesbank council met for its regular policy-meeting on Wednesday with its agenda topped by a plan to revalue its assets.
German finance minister Theo Waigel two weeks ago announced his aim of revaluing the central bank's gold and foreign exchange holdings in a bid to raise money for cash-strapped Bonn budgets.
Financial markets will be looking closely at the Bundesbank statement to assess the level of support the central bank is giving to the Bonn plan.
Waigel's scheme has already unsettled some who say the move will pave the way for a weak single European currency.
The revaluation plan is part of proposals by Waigel to shore up Germany's 1997 budget, straining to meet Maastricht criteria for European monetary union (EMU).
